Orbital Ember – AI-Powered Space Fire Safety Research Dashboard

Orbital Ember is an AI-powered research dashboard developed to make NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion research easier to explore, understand, and analyze. NASA has collected decades of experimental data about how fire behaves in microgravity, but the large volume of scientific records and datasets makes it difficult for researchers to find relevant information and interpret results.

Our project addresses this challenge by providing a centralized platform to search NASA investigations, explore research data, download datasets, and analyze experimental results. It also features an AI research assistant that uses a locally running language model to answer questions and generate summaries based on available research sources. A custom scenario feature allows users to explore different conditions, including oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, gravity, material, and thickness.

By making complex scientific information more accessible, Orbital Ember aims to support research into spacecraft fire hazards and contribute to safer future space missions.

Orbital Ember – Project Details

Problem Statement

NASA has conducted numerous combustion experiments to understand fire behavior in microgravity. However, the enormous amount of scientific data stored in the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository makes it difficult for researchers to locate relevant investigations, compare experimental results, and extract useful fire-safety information.

This creates a challenge when designing safer spacecraft, lunar habitats, and future space exploration missions.

Our Solution

Orbital Ember is a local research dashboard that combines NASA research data, dataset analysis, and artificial intelligence into one platform. It helps users discover relevant investigations and understand scientific information without manually searching through large amounts of research documentation.

Main Features

1. AI Research Assistant

  • Allows users to ask questions about combustion research.
  • Generates short explanations and research summaries.
  • Uses a locally running AI model through Ollama.
  • Supports offline AI functionality without requiring cloud-based AI services.

2. NASA PSI Research Explorer

  • Searches NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics investigation catalogue.
  • Displays investigation information and related research files.
  • Supports filtering research by flammability, detection, suppression, and fundamental research.
  • Maintains an offline copy of the investigation index.

3. Dataset Analysis

  • Supports CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL, and ZIP datasets.
  • Displays row and column counts.
  • Identifies missing values.
  • Calculates numerical statistics such as minimum, maximum, mean, and median.
  • Shows categorical frequencies, data previews, and simple trend plots.

4. Custom Scenario Analysis
Users can provide different experimental conditions, including:

  • Material type.
  • Oxygen concentration.
  • Atmospheric pressure.
  • Airflow speed.
  • Gravity level.
  • Material thickness.

The AI assistant uses these conditions as context when discussing relevant research. This is an exploratory research feature, not a validated fire-risk prediction system.

5. Offline Data Archive

  • Stores NASA investigation metadata locally.
  • Maintains a bounded archive of research files with a 12 GB storage limit.
  • Supports downloading research files in batches.
  • Refreshes investigation information from NASA when internet access is available.
  • Keeps existing research accessible when offline.

Technologies Used

  • Python for backend development and data processing.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface.
  • FastAPI for backend API services.
  • Ollama for locally running AI.
  • Llama 3.2 (1B) as the language model.
  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics as the primary research data source.

Project Impact

Orbital Ember makes scientific research more accessible by combining research discovery, data analysis, and AI-assisted explanations. It can help students, researchers, and aerospace engineers explore combustion experiments and identify research relevant to spacecraft fire safety.

The long-term goal is to support better-informed decisions when developing fire detection systems, suppression technologies, and safer materials for spacecraft and future lunar habitats.
